claims.statement: `local-proof` is a thin orchestration over primitives that already exist (git validation, index projection, retrieval, and a `commit_note` dry run) and deliberately provisions no endpoints, clients, or services, so local recall is proven before any endpoint concept enters the flow.

`run_local_proof` requires exactly one target: passing both a repo path and `--demo-dir` raises `ambiguous_target`, and passing neither raises `missing_target`, each with a message and concrete next action instead of a stack trace.

Existing-vault local proof is read-only by default — it creates no sample content and no commit unless `--seed-sample` is explicit — while demo mode builds a dedicated tiny git-backed vault and refuses a populated directory that is not already a git repo.

A successful proof returns a stable contract: `status: local_memory_works`, the fixed six-milestone vocabulary (`git_vault_confirmed` through `dry_run_write_previewed`), the repo-relative `source_path`, retrieval hit, dry-run `write_preview`, index info, `files_are_source_of_truth: true`, a `next_action`, and `error: null`.

A failed proof degrades the same contract (`status: needs_action`, empty milestones, `source_path: null`, `error.code` from a fixed set) and the CLI prints the message plus next action to stderr and exits 1 with no traceback.

The proof builds the disposable projection at `<repo>/.hypermnesic/index.db` (state dir `0700`, database `0600`, `.hypermnesic/` added to `.git/info/exclude`), projects committed content only, and retries the catch-up lexically when the embedder raises.

The default proof is lexical-only (no API key required) and dense is opt-in via `--dense`; `degraded_lexical_only` is set from search degradation, a `no-git` catch-up, or an absent embedder, and always carries a product-language message rather than an error.

Every string the proof echoes is sanitized first — bearer tokens, `sk-`-shaped keys, approval-token assignments, and operator home paths are redacted — and paths are reported repo-relative only, so the vault's absolute path never leaves the contract.

When `--query` is omitted the proof derives one: demo mode uses a fixed demo question, and an existing vault scans committed markdown for a `Question answered:` line, falls back to the first line of at least three words truncated to 160 characters, and finally to the demo question.

`doctor` and `status` are one command behind two parser names and are strictly non-mutating: they start no service, rewrite no configuration, create no tokens, change no routes, touch no vault content, and create no commit — verified by watching git `HEAD`, the vault file list, the absent `--env-file` file, and mutating `SetupOps` calls.

Each diagnostic check carries an id, a category (`local`, `remote`, `oauth`, `auth`, `write`), one of four statuses (`pass`, `warn`, `skipped`, `fail`) with a derived severity, a summary, and a `next_action` with a stable code, optional command, and doc pointer; skipped checks are reported as skipped with their reason rather than passing silently.

Without `--public-url` every remote, OAuth, auth, and write check is reported `skipped` with the `provide_public_url` action and no HTTP call is made at all (discovery verification is never invoked), so local diagnosis works offline.

The overall diagnostic status is `needs_attention` only when some check is `fail`; `warn` and `skipped` never block it, and `what_this_means` either states that local memory is healthy enough with no blocking remote failure or names the first failing check's summary.

Dense state is derived in a fixed order: an unreadable repo `.env` short-circuits to a `fail` with `repair_key_file`; a discovered key is `configured_unverified` unless `--check-dense-live` distinguishes `configured_valid` from `configured_invalid`; and readable vector coverage then replaces the credential state with `vectors_stale_or_absent` or `index_missing_or_unbuilt` while preserving `configured_invalid`.

The dense remedies are state-specific: `index_missing_or_unbuilt` points at `hypermnesic local-proof /path/to/vault` to build the projection, while `vectors_stale_or_absent` points at `hypermnesic converge /path/to/vault --now --json` rather than a full reindex.

The local index check is deliberately three-way — missing (`fail`), present but possibly lagging `HEAD` (`warn`), or current enough — and exposes the raw `fresh` boolean in `detail`, treating an uncomparable vault with no `HEAD` as not stale rather than failing.

Given `--env-file PATH`, the consent-secret check reports only whether the file exists and whether its permissions are owner-only (`0600`); it never reads or prints the value, a broader mode is a `warn` with a `chmod 600` remedy, and omitting the path yields a `skipped` check with the `provide_env_file` action.

One shared secret-free client guidance map serves both commands — doctor returns it as `next_actions` and setup as `client_next_actions` — covering the local CLI and Obsidian companion as always available and the generic remote MCP client and Claude Code / Codex plugin as available only once a public URL is known.

`setup` is fail-closed and ordered so that all preflight work happens before any side effect: resolving the token TTL, refusing a non-HTTPS or bare-IP public origin or resource, normalizing the default client scopes against the supported set, confirming the target is a git repo, confirming the engine credential is discoverable, and confirming Tailscale is installed and running — any failure raises `InstallError` with nothing created.

After the routes are applied `setup` verifies the live HTTPS discovery chain by real output — RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, RFC 8414 AS metadata carrying a `token_endpoint`, and an unauthenticated POST that must answer 401 — and fails the command when a well-known does not resolve to this service.

The setup side effects are a consent secret persisted into an owner-only (`0600`) env file (default `~/.config/hypermnesic-cloud/cloud.env`, minted with `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` and required to clear the 24-character entropy floor), a rendered cloud unit installed and started under `~/.config/systemd/user`, and the per-mount funnel routes for the MCP mount plus both root discovery well-knowns.

The rendered cloud unit references `EnvironmentFile` for the repo `.env` and the owner-only cloud env file, so the approval token and `OPENAI_API_KEY` values are never inlined, and the unsuffixed host-root `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` is intentionally absent from the routes to avoid a co-tenant collision.
Route application always shells out to `tailscale funnel --set-path` and never `tailscale serve`, because `serve --set-path` silently clears the funnel allowance and drops public reach.

`setup` re-running converges: a consent secret at or above the entropy floor is reused untouched (regenerated only when absent or weak), the unit is re-rendered so a changed or newly defaulted `--token-ttl` lands, and the declarative de-duplicated funnel route set is re-applied to the same mounts.

`setup` renders the same serving knobs as the lane it starts: `--token-ttl` (default `172800` / 48 h, overridable by env or flag), `--default-client-scopes` (default `read`, resolved from the flag or `HYPERMNESIC_DEFAULT_CLIENT_SCOPES`), and a repeatable `--allowlist` that narrows the write surface.

Requesting the write scope by default changes only what new clients ask for: the consent page still requires the operator approval token and remote write still cannot bypass protected paths, frontmatter validation, dirty-tree checks, head-drift checks, audit logging, or git guards.

`install` provisions a host into one of three roles (`single`, `master`, `client`), rejects an unknown role against the known set, and is pure, offline, and idempotent — it verifies the environment, renders artifacts, writes the role config, and installs the convergence hook while returning host-specific side effects as manual steps.

For the engine roles the diagnostic-relevant artifact set is one service artifact per flavor (a systemd unit, or a Dockerfile plus `compose.yaml`), a role config at `<repo>/.hypermnesic/config.json` recording role, bind, port, path, `write_enabled`, and service, and the post-merge hook, with `hypermnesic init` plus the service-enable or compose commands returned as manual steps.
Bind rules are enforced at provision time: a wildcard bind (`0.0.0.0`, `::`, empty) is refused, `single` forces `127.0.0.1`, and `master` requires an explicit `--bind`.

Both the rendered unit and the installed hook use an absolute executable path resolved as `shutil.which` first, then the console script next to the running interpreter, then the bare name, because `systemctl --user` runs the unit without the project venv on `PATH`; a test asserts the rendered `ExecStart` path is absolute and exists.

Role provisioning renders a write-enabled serve, and the engine enforces `write_enabled ⇒ auth-required` at startup for any non-loopback bind unless the operator passes the explicit CGNAT-bounded `--allow-tailnet-write` opt-in; a loopback bind is exempt as the local drop-in.

When auth parameters are supplied to the master render they are shlex-quoted onto `ExecStart` with repeatable `--required-scope`, while the resource-server introspection credentials stay in the environment rather than the unit.

The client role requires `--master-url` and `--mcp-config` and only upserts one MCP client entry: other servers are preserved, a malformed `mcpServers` map is reset to a dict rather than raising, and with auth parameters the entry becomes OAuth2-aware carrying a `token_env` pointer to `HYPERMNESIC_MCP_TOKEN` instead of any token value.

The convergence hook is written as one delimited managed block whose command is the shlex-quoted executable running `converge` against the shlex-quoted repo, redirected and terminated with `|| true` so a convergence hiccup can never fail a `git pull`; the hook-name tuple is extensible without changing the contract.

Hook installation is idempotent (re-running leaves exactly one managed block), non-destructive (operator content before and after the block is preserved and a missing hook is created with a shebang), makes the hook executable, and uninstall removes only the managed block — deleting the file when nothing but a bare shebang remains and keeping content when a block has no closing marker.

Engine-role provisioning installs the managed post-merge hook internally, and `hypermnesic install-hooks` is the explicit opt-in path, while `setup` does not install hooks — it renders the cloud unit and routes only; the hook remains acceleration, since lazy read-time convergence is the correctness guarantee.

A version or provisioning change must keep `scripts/check_version_consistency.py` green; `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` is the authority and the gate names every mirror that must agree, so the mirrors are never hand-enumerated.

Anything committed about provisioning must use placeholders rather than operator values — `scripts/preflight_public_scan.py` fails on operator tailnet names, homelab IPs, inline token values, credential material, and operator home paths, so docs and fixtures use forms like `<your-host>.ts.net` and the `100.64.0.0/10` CGNAT range.

The deterministic local product smoke loop ends with a `doctor_status` stage that runs the diagnostics against the fixture vault, so the diagnostic contract is exercised by the readiness smoke as well as by unit tests.
